findings.title: AO neighbor sampling uses face normal instead of tangent directions
findings.detail: The AO calculation uses d[0],d[1],d[2] (face normal) as tangent offsets for getBlock() calls. For a top face (d=[0,1,0]), s1=getBlock(vx2+0,vy2,vz2+0) checks the same block position — always air — so top/bottom faces always get AO=1.0 (no occlusion). For side faces, the normal direction is checked instead of the two perpendicular tangent axes. This makes AO shading wrong for every face orientation.

findings.title: Particle drag is frame-rate dependent
findings.detail: p.vx*=0.95; p.vz*=0.95; is applied per frame without scaling by dt. At 60fps this reduces velocity to ~4.6%/s; at 30fps it is ~21.5%/s. Particles decelerate at different rates depending on frame rate.
